newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Diesel remains actively traded.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Diesel remains actively traded.

text.p: The gas oil market continued to be actively traded on Friday with 450,000 barrels done, after 760,000 barrels exchanged hands a day earlier, traders said.
They said a Japanese trader bought all three cargoes ranging between $27.50 and $28.75 a barrel free-on-board (fob) basis for early to second-half April lifting.
Two cargoes were sold by a European major and one by a French oil company.
Traders said the cargoes would eventually be absorbed by a Singapore trader who would have bought over four million barrels with these purchases.

They said a U.S. major last week purchased 300,000 barrels of gas oil from a Swiss trader at 40-45 cents per barrel over Singapore spot quotes for April 5-10 arrival, cost-and-freight Singapore basis.
A European major also sold last week 20,000 tonnes to a German trader at 40 cents per barrel over Singapore quotes, for end April lifting fob Singapore.
Traders said the European major would ship in a 130,000-tonne cargo of gas oil and a 60,000-tonne jet fuel cargo from the Middle East for first half April arrival.
The major also noted that the 200,000 barrels it bought from a Chinese bunker trader was partly sold to a Singapore trader rather than to cover its short into India.

Traders said the bulk of offers into Indian Oil Corp's (IOC) tender to buy May gas oil were based on Mediterranean quotes with east coast cargoes ranging between $28.00 and $30.00 a tonne premium and west cost cargoes between $24.00 and $28.50 premium.
India was expected to take about 500,000 tonnes of diesel, but some optimistic projections placed it at 700,000-800,000 tonnes.
Indonesia's gas oil demand for April is projected at between 3.5 million and 4.0 million barrels.
Jet fuel was actively offered within Thursday's range with three sellers seen at between $27.00 and $27.25 per barrel for second half April lifting fob. But buyers stayed aloof.
Gas oil swaps rose along with the sustained strength seen on physical cargoes. April swaps gaied 25 cents a barrel, to $26.65/$26.75, with the regrade maintaining Thursday's 30/40 cents level.
